newsitem.title: UK: Benign U.S. inflation data reassures bourses.
newsitem.headline: Benign U.S. inflation data reassures bourses.

text.p: Benign U.S. inflation data on Thursday cooled market speculation of an imminent credit tightening, helped Wall Street open higher and provided some reassurance for European bourses.

London's blue-chip FTSE 100 share index cut its losses and climbed to the day's highest levels -- though still well into negative territory -- after the Dow Jones industrial average opened up 11 points and moved higher.
The Dow took heart from Labor Department data showing the crucial core producer price rate rate, which excludes fuel and food, was up only 0.1 percent in December, in line with forecasts.

The Paris bourse, which had been trading most of the day in the red, also rose into plus figures and Frankfurt's IBIS DAX electronic trading index hit a new record. German floor trading had closed earlier about half a percent down.

In currency trading, the dollar fell back from a two-year high against the mark and was slightly weaker against the yen after the data, which was interpreted as meaning there was less pressure for an early, dollar-boosting, U.S. rate hike.

Earlier, the dollar had touched a new two-year high just above 1.58 marks after German data showed a surge in unemployment during December to a postwar high as well as weaker-than -expected 1996 economic growth, widening the country's budget deficit.
The figures increased speculation that German rates would be trimmed again at some stage but Thursday's regular meeting of the Bundesbank council, as expected, held rates steady.
By mid-afternoon the dollar had slipped back to around 1.5735 marks.

One concern for mark bulls was the health of Russian president Boris Yeltsin, who has been admitted to hospital with pneumonia. Any threat of instability in Russia tends to have a negative effect on the German currency.

Yen weakness was intensified by a continuing freefall overnight in Tokyo stocks, which have slid 11.5 percent since mid-December. The latest tumble was sparked by worries that major banks might not solve their huge debt problems amid broader concerns about the health of the Japanese economy.
In morning European trading the dollar was quoted at 116.22 yen, up from 115.90 late on Wednesday, but by mid-afternoon, after the U.S. price data, it slipped to around 116.06.

Boosted by the Dow, leading London shares recovered some of their losses but were still down around a third of a percent by 1530 GMT and dealers said interest rate worries were still damaging sentiment.

"The bond markets are telling us that British interest rates need to be a half-point higher," said Richard Jeffrey, strategist at Charterhouse Tilney. "The market needs to know what will happen with rates."

German shares were little moved by the jobless data but dealers said overnight weakness on Wall Street was holding the market down. The DAX index pared some of its losses but still closed floor trade nearly 14 points down.
It was not until Wall Street reopened higher that the IBIS DAX index for screen trading took some heart from New York and moved ahead more than half a percent, scoring a new record high.

It was a similar story in Paris, where stocks firmed on the back of Wall Street in the afternoon. The announcement of Societe Generale's planned purchase of Credit du Nord from Paribas was a focus of attention, keeping merger interest alive.
CURRENCIES AT 1530 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.5735 marks and 116.06 yen compared with 1.5758 and 115.90 late in Europe on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1530 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares was down 10.2 points to 4,077.7.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed floor trade down 13.71 at 2,892.63 but the IBIS DAX index was up 17.17 points at 2,921.25, surpassing its previous record peak of 2,916.6 set on December 5.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 15.39 at 2,347.01.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $356.50 in the afternoon, compared with its London close of $355.75 on Wednesday. Silver was firmer with gold at $4.72.
